summary: The submitted solution is not a real implementation of Two Sum: it returns a hardcoded pair and does not use the input array or target. As a result, it only passes a small subset of tests and fails basic and edge cases, indicating the core algorithm was not implemented within the session time.

primary_focus: Implement the canonical single-pass hash-map Two Sum pattern (check complement before inserting) instead of hardcoding outputs.
thinking_and_logic: The final submission does not reflect an implemented algorithm: it iterates over indices but performs no work inside the loop and returns a constant answer. This explains the observed failures on basic placements (e.g., pair at end) and edge conditions (negatives, empty input), because the output is unrelated to nums/target.
code_assessment: Compared to the answer key’s optimal solution (single pass with a hash map of seen values -> index), the submitted code misses the core technique entirely and therefore cannot generalize beyond a coincidentally-correct visible test. The canonical approach achieves O(n) time and reliably avoids using the same element twice by checking the complement among previously seen indices before inserting the current element; your code neither checks complements nor tracks indices.

next_steps.action: Write the optimal single-pass hash-map solution from memory (value->index; for each i,x: if target-x in map return [map[target-x], i]; else map[x]=i).
next_steps.why: This is the canonical solution in the answer key and matches the constraint scale (n up to 1e5) with O(n) time.
next_steps.how: Practice implementing it 5 times in a row without looking; each time, test mentally on: nums=[2,7,11,15],target=9; nums=[3,2,4],target=6; nums=[-1,-2,-3,-4,-5],target=-8.

next_steps.action: Add a quick self-check routine before submission: run through at least one 'pair at end' and one 'negative numbers' example by hand.
next_steps.why: Your failures map directly to not validating behavior beyond the simplest case.
next_steps.how: After coding, simulate 4-5 iterations on paper and confirm when/why the return triggers and that indices are distinct.

next_steps.action: Clarify edge-case behavior up front (e.g., empty input) and match it to expected tests.
next_steps.why: One failing test expects [] for empty input; handling this explicitly prevents avoidable failures.
next_steps.how: Start the function with `if len(nums) < 2: return []` (or the contract required by the platform), then proceed with the main algorithm.

interview habit: baseline correctness first, then optimize
encouragement: Once you consistently implement the hash-map complement pattern, this problem becomes very routine—focus on getting a fully working general solution rather than a placeholder return.
